full_judgment:
10. The learned counsel finally contends that, since the mother of the present opposite party Nos. 2-3 by adopting the written statement so filed by her predecessor including other defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit so there has been no scope to pass a decree in favour of the defendant No. 3(kha) and 3(ga) even providing saham to the mother of the opposite party Nos. 2-3 that is, the petitioner as prayed for in the subsequent written statement. However, in support of his submission, the learned counsel has placed his reliance in the decisions reported AIR 1952 MB 207, AIR 1943 Cal 613 AIR 1924 Mad 245 and AIR 2003 Raj 306 and by reading out the relevant paragraphs the learned counsel then contends that, in all those decisions it has been settled that there has been no scope on the part of the heirs of any parties to suit to deviate from the stand taken by their predecessor and therefore the learned judge of the trial court has erroneously allowed the written statement as well as application for amendment to the said written statement and then prayed for making the Rule absolute on setting aside the impugned judgment and order. 

 11. On the contrary, Mr. Sk. Md. Jahangir Alam, the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 very robustly opposes the contention so taken by the learned counsel for the petitioner and mainly submits that, if the suit is not decreed, there has been no scope to give saham to the defendant No. 3(kha) and 3(ga) and therefore the learned judge has rightly passed the impugned order in favour of the defendant No. 3(kha) and 3(ga) allowing the written statement as well as the application for amendment of the written statement. 

 12. The learned counsel finally contends that, since the suit has not yet been disposed of so none of the parties can say whether the suit will be decreed or dismissed so at that stage it is premature to submit that the defendant has deviated from their earlier stand asserted in their written statement filed by their predecessor and finally prays for discharging the Rule.
